basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 36.' and it opens '(Vers. 36 et seqq.) Et conceperunt duae filiae Lot de patre suo, et genuit primogenita'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 36 et seqq.) Et conceperunt duae filiae Lot de patre suo, et genuit primogenita filium, et vocavit nomen ejus Moab. Iste est pater Moabitarum usque in hanc diem. Et minor, et ipsa peperit filium, et vocavit nomen ejus Ammon id est, filius populi mei. Ipse est pater filiorum Ammon. Moab interpretatur, ex patre: et totum nomen etymologiam habet. Ammon vero, cujus quasi causa nominis redditur, filius generis mei, sive ut melius est in Hebraeo (עמי), filius populi mei, sic derivatur, ut ex parte sensus nominis, ex parte ipse sit sermo: AMMI enim, a quo dicti sunt Ammonitae, vocatur populus meus.
